Jarvis-Voice-Assistant.body:
# 🔧 Add `uninstall.sh` Script for Safe and Complete Removal of Jarvis (Fixes #5)

## Description

This pull request adds a new `uninstall.sh` script to address [Issue #5](https://github.com/your-repo-link/issues/5), enabling users to safely and completely uninstall the Jarvis AI voice assistant and all its associated files, dependencies, and configurations.

---

## 🛠️ Key Features of `uninstall.sh`

- 🔐 **Interactive confirmation prompts** to prevent accidental data loss  
- 🗂️ **Removes user data** (e.g., notes, voice recordings, webcam photos)  
- 🧹 **Cleans up generated files** and AI cache  
- 🧠 **Deletes downloaded models** like Vosk and Piper TTS  
- 🧪 **Uninstalls Python virtual environment** and all Python dependencies  
- ⚙️ **Removes configuration files** including API keys, contacts, and face data  
- 🛠️ **Optionally removes system packages**: `ffmpeg`, `rofi`, `mpv`, `alsa-utils`  
- 🚨 **Safety validations** to prevent unintended deletions  
- 💾 **Option to preserve** important files (like API keys or contacts)  

---

## 🧪 Tested On:

- ✅ Ubuntu 22.04  
- ✅ Arch Linux (Hyprland)

---

This script enhances user control and flexibility, offering a full rollback option for those who wish to uninstall Jarvis — especially useful for testers, contributors, and developers.

> After running `uninstall.sh`, users may optionally delete the entire project directory using:  
> ```bash
> rm -rf /path/to/jarvis-voice-assistant
> ```

## Documentation Overhaul and New Content

### Description
This PR includes a structural overhaul of the documentation and the addition of new content and tested examples.

### Key Changes
- **Started moving /api content to /archive**: Initiated migration of all legacy API content to `/archive`. Once everything is successfully reorganized, `/archive` will be removed entirely.
- **Reorganized protocol documentation**: Grouped and relocated protocol-specific docs (HTTP, WebSocket, TCP, UDP) into their respective sections:
  - `http/`
  - `websocket/`
  - `tcp/`
  - `udp/`
- **Added Guides/Interactive TCP Shell**: Created a new guide to showcase the interactive TCP CLI.
  - Includes step-by-step usage.
  - Verified functionality using a custom `echo_server.py` (also included and referenced).
- **Introduced Command-Line Interface/Overview**: Serves as a high-level intro to CLI structure and protocol groupings.
- Additional enhancements planned in future updates.

### Next Steps
- Continue migrating/refining `archive/` content.
- Expand `cli/index.md` with more command detail and real-world use cases.
- Add more guides and examples for the interactive shell and protocol clients.

### Testing & Review
- The interactive TCP shell works as documented.
- You can test doc rendering locally by running `make serve`.
- All `reference.md` pages should now include Google-style docstrings via `mkdocstrings`.
- Please review the new structure and content organization. Let me know if any navigation or naming refinements would help clarify the new layout.

No protection against DoS attacks, making servers vulnerable to abuse.

- New module: `kn_sock/rate_limit.py`

kn-sock.title: Fix inconsistent error handling in TCP/UDP modules
kn-sock.body:
# Standardize Error Handling Across Socket Operations

## Background
Currently, some socket functions catch exceptions silently while others propagate them, causing inconsistent behavior across the codebase.

## Files to Modify
- `kn_sock/tcp.py`
- `kn_sock/udp.py`

## Expected Outcome
- All socket operations should implement consistent error handling.
- Exceptions should be properly propagated rather than silently caught.
- This will improve reliability and debuggability of socket operations.
